threads.body: Package-private visibility is fine here for JUnit 5, which discovers test methods via reflection (`setAccessible(true)`) regardless of visibility. The RxJava 3 sibling (`AbstractRxJava3SubscriptionTest`) already uses this same pattern successfully, so this aligns well. Just worth knowing that this works because of JUnit 5 reflective discovery, not Java inheritance, since concrete subclasses in other packages won't inherit package-private methods through normal Java semantics.

Switching from `hasAttributes(attributeEntry(...))` to `hasAttributesSatisfyingExactly(equalTo(longKey("iteration"), iteration))` is strictly correct for spans you fully control ("outer", "middle", "inner" are user-created via `runWithSpan`). One thing to confirm: `iteration` appears to be typed as `int` in the enclosing loop. The call `equalTo(longKey("iteration"), iteration)` relies on widening from `int` to `long` at the primitive level, which Java handles automatically. If `iteration` were ever declared as `Integer` (boxed), you would get a generic type mismatch with `AttributeKey<Long>`. The current pattern is fine as-is, but casting to `(long) iteration` would make the intent explicit and guard against future refactoring.
